pointers.sentence: `LazySettings` is a `LazyObject`, Django's general lazy proxy, which holds what it stands for in `LazyObject._wrapped`, the marker `empty` until a subclass's `_setup` method puts something there ([Lazy objects: `LazyObject` and `SimpleLazyObject`](../utils/lazy-objects.md)) (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject`).

If the variable is unset or empty it raises `ImproperlyConfigured`, with a message that names the setting that was being read; otherwise it makes a `Settings` from the module's name and wraps it (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._setup`).

And code that may run before there are settings can ask without loading them: the property `LazySettings.configured` is true when something is wrapped, and reading it loads nothing (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.configured`).
`Signal.connect`, run as modules are imported, tests it before it reads `settings.DEBUG` to decide whether to validate the receiver (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.connect`).

A model's class statement asks the app registry which application it belongs to, and the registry reads `settings.INSTALLED_APPS` before it refuses with `AppRegistryNotReady`, so that missing settings are reported as such ([The registry and its models](registry.md#a-model-class-registers-itself)) (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.check_apps_ready`).
Its constructor fills it in two layers, and refuses, warns about or acts on a few of the values (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).
First it copies every upper-case name of `django/conf/global_settings.py` onto itself.

Five settings must each be a list or a tuple, or `ImproperlyConfigured` is raised: `"ALLOWED_HOSTS"`, `"INSTALLED_APPS"`, `"LOCALE_PATHS"`, `"SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS"` and `"TEMPLATE_DIRS"`, which 1.10 removed as a setting and the constructor tests still (`docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

The settings 6.1 deprecated that the module defines are each warned about with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, and a deprecated email setting defined beside `MAILERS` is refused instead (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`).
The settings module that `django-admin startproject` writes defines `MAILERS` (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`).

The move is made only where `time` has `"tzset"`, and the comment at that line says why by its ticket: "See ticket #2315 for why we don't do this unconditionally (breaks Windows)" (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

`django/conf/global_settings.py` is a module of plain assignments, and it has to stay one: it is imported by `django.conf` itself, before there are settings, so it can import nothing that reads a setting.

The translation functions are such a thing, which is why the module defines a function of its own, `gettext_noop`, that returns its argument, to mark the names of languages for translation (`django/conf/global_settings.py:gettext_noop`).
Not every setting has a default there: `ROOT_URLCONF` has none, and where the project does not set it either, reading it raises `AttributeError` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

`global_settings` assigns it the very list it assigns to `ADMINS`, an empty one: it is computed from the default, once, and a project that sets `ADMINS` has not thereby set `MANAGERS` (`django/conf/global_settings.py:MANAGERS`).
The method therefore ends by storing the value it found in the proxy's own instance dictionary, under the setting's name (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

`MEDIA_URL` and `STATIC_URL`, when they are relative, have the script prefix put in front of them: a value that begins with neither a slash nor `"http://"` or `"https://"` is joined to what `get_script_prefix` returns at that moment, and the joined value is what is kept (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._add_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:get_script_prefix`).

`MEDIA_URL` and `STATIC_URL`, when they are relative, have the script prefix put in front of them: a value that begins with neither a slash nor `"http://"` or `"https://"` is joined to what `get_script_prefix` returns at that moment, and the joined value is what is kept (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._add_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:get_script_prefix`).
The documentation says that a relative `STATIC_URL` or `MEDIA_URL` is prefixed by the server-provided value of `"SCRIPT_NAME"` (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).

It is prefixed by the script prefix in force at its first read, and kept: a later read returns that value whatever the prefix has become, until a write through the proxy drops it (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__setattr__`, `django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__delattr__`).

A read of a deprecated email setting is intercepted here too: it raises `AttributeError` where `MAILERS` is defined, and otherwise warns only a reader outside Django, so that Django's own compatibility code reads it in silence ([Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md#without-mailers-the-deprecated-settings)) (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`).
Assigning a new wrapped object clears every kept value at once (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__setattr__`).
Deleting a setting removes its kept value in the same way (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__delattr__`).

A process can supply its settings directly, with no module and no environment variable, by calling `LazySettings.configure` before anything reads a setting (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.configure`).

It keeps only the names set on it, and a read of any other upper-case name not deleted falls through to a second object, its `default_settings`: for `configure` the `global_settings` module unless the caller passes another, for an override the object wrapped before it ([Overriding settings](overrides.md)) (`django/conf/__init__.py:UserSettingsHolder.__getattr__`).
A deprecated email setting given beside `MAILERS` is refused all the same (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.configure`).
